note: Everything in game/ that is drawn or played without a recorded asset. Placeholders stand in for production assets and name the milestone that removes them. Functional entries are particles, UI and debug drawing, which Bible 15 does not count as placeholders. tests/test_placeholders.gd fails when a primitive, code-built, saved or referenced mesh in game/**/*.gd, .tscn or .tres, or a binary resource or model file anywhere in game/, is not listed here by type and file, and when a placeholder's asset_id has a record in assets/records.

placeholders.description: The creature editor's ground disc: a flat CylinderMesh under the creature, dark blue with a soft pool of light at its centre and an edge that feathers out (editor_floor.gdshader), scaled to the body, so the Spore-style room has a floor until the creature-stage art pass gives the editor a modelled room.
The creature stage's test field: a flat 160 x 160 m PlaneMesh in a plain green material, until the creature stage art pass brings terrain and ground cover (creature-stage-plan.md section 5).
The nest at the field's centre: a flat TorusMesh ring at the nest radius (6 m), the only place the creature can evolve, until the art pass models a nest.
Fruit bushes: 40 SphereMesh instances in one MultiMesh, red and full when ripe, small and green while regrowing, until the art pass models bushes.
Meat left where a creature dies: a small BoxMesh in one MultiMesh, until the art pass models a carcass.

functional.description: Draw mesh of the CPUParticles3D eat burst (at most 12 particles).
Pooled Label3D for meal toasts such as "+8 energy", the "Regrowing" labels and the "−12" hit numbers. Text, not geometry.
Debug builds only: zone rings, resolver mouth arcs and the reach circle drawn as lines.

The strike lane of a tell on the player: a unit quad scaled to CreatureBrain.strike_lane() with threat_lane.gdshader (the inside at alpha 0.25 at most, the thin outline at 0.7). Gameplay UI drawn on the swim plane, not a model. creature_view.gd builds one more unit quad with the lane's material for the start fade's shader warm-up, drawn out of sight.
Label3D "!" over a creature for 0.6 s when it notices the cell. Text, not geometry.
Label3D "Dodged!" rising over the cell for 0.8 s when a strike on it ends without a hit. Text, not geometry.
A full-screen ColorRect with hurt_vignette.gdshader: a dark red glow at the screen edges, one pulse per hit on the cell (alpha at most 0.35, gone in 0.4 s). Gameplay UI, not a model.

Off-screen threat arrows drawn with CanvasItem draw calls: a badge with the species glyph (HudIcon jaw or star) and a pointer on the screen edge, pulsing with "!" during a tell. Gameplay UI, not a model.

The fluid's opaque bottom: a 400 x 400 m PlaneMesh 40 m under the swim plane with backdrop.gdshader (unshaded, engine fog on). The height fog covers it to 97%, so every pixel shows only the fog colour at that depth and no shape of its own; it is the background that art's decor fades into, not a model (micro-world plan section 3).

The sunlit patches: one unit PlaneMesh, scaled to a disc 2.6 zone radii across under each plankton zone, carrying zone_light.gdshader's soft shafts of cream light, blended round the zone's edge (micro-world plan C7). Light with no shape of its own, not a model.

Camera-facing quads of the pool ambience: drifting specks, bubbles and microbe swarms drawn by drift.gdshader (about 1,560 instances in three MultiMeshes), and ten flat quads carrying the pre-blurred backdrop organisms rendered by tools/blender/make_ambience_backdrops.py. Decor that never collides; the quad is only a carrier for a shader or texture. The PlaneMesh reference is the quad's orientation constant.

The title world's copy of fluid_backdrop: the same 400 x 400 m PlaneMesh 40 m under the swim plane with backdrop.gdshader, so the title's sea fades into the same fog colour as the pool's. No shape of its own, not a model.

The creature stage's generated skin: a Surface Nets ArrayMesh built at runtime from the body description's capsule field (game/systems/creature/skin_cpu.gd or skin_gpu.gd), skinned to the generated Skeleton3D with CUSTOM0 paint coordinates and CUSTOM1 rest positions, drawn with the art team's creature_skin.gdshader. Spore-style full-body building (docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-10-23): the player's anatomy is the model, so there is no Blender source for it. The art parts on it are the recorded cpart_* assets.

The creature editor's handles and gizmos: unshaded SphereMesh instances on every vertebra, joint and part of the working body (orange, blue, green; the selection brighter and larger) and the selected part's turn ring drawn as an ImmediateMesh line strip. Editing UI drawn in the 3D view, not a model.
